label: rem:leray-profile-construction
title: Construction of the truncated $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$ Leray system
html:
Remark. Construction of the truncated \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Leray system

The Leray rescaling. In Leray's similarity variables y = (x - x_0)/\sqrt{T^* - t}, s = -\log(T^* - t), the velocity profile satisfies the Leray system. A continuous self-similar blowup would require a time-independent (s-independent) profile (V, P) on \mathbb{R}^3 with V \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3); every such nontrivial finite-energy profile is trivial [necas-ruzicka-sverak1996], a no-go extended to local-energy estimates [tsai1998]. The admissible profile is therefore discretely self-similar — periodic in s — with period fixed by the root-of-unity scaling \lambda_\kappa.

The \mathrm{SU}_q(2) decomposition. By the Peter--Weyl theorem, the profile decomposes into matrix coefficients. The Leray equations decompose by spin. The nonlinear coupling coefficients are determined by the Clebsch--Gordan decomposition.

Truncation by the discrete spectrum. The discrete vortex spectrum eigenvalues grow exponentially in j. The centrifugal barrier suppresses high-spin components. At the physical value q \approx 1.110, we have k_{\max} \approx 4 active modes. The discretely self-similar profile is a finite sum.

The truncated Leray system. Substituting the truncated ansatz gives a system of 5 coupled ODEs in the radial variable r, the s-periodicity being carried by the ansatz coefficients.

Boundary conditions. Regularity at r \to 0 requires R_j(r) \sim r^{\ell_j}. Square-integrability at r \to \infty requires R_j(r) = O(r^{-5/2}).

The nonlinear coupling matrix. The fusion rules constrain which spin interactions drive the blowup. The dominant interaction is the j = 1/2 \otimes 1/2 \to 0 channel: two fundamental vortices fuse into the trivial representation, releasing energy into radial compression.

The fundamental profile (j = 1/2 only). The simplest nontrivial ansatz retains only j = 1/2. This yields a second-order nonlinear ODE with two boundary conditions. The nonlinear eigenvalue problem has a discrete spectrum of solutions.

Open question. The existence of a nontrivial discretely self-similar solution to the truncated Leray ODE is a finite-dimensional shooting problem; the continuous (s-independent) case is excluded [necas-ruzicka-sverak1996], so any solution must carry genuine s-periodicity. The QOU contribution is the finite truncation: the classical Leray equations are infinite-dimensional, but \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation theory reduces them to a finite system of ODEs.
